A comprehensive guide to mobile app development companies in Jeddah, key criteria for choosing the best tech partner, app types, and costs in Saudi Arabia.

Designing a mobile app has become an important step for companies that want to deliver their services more easily, reach customers, and develop new revenue streams. However, an app’s success depends on more than programming alone; it starts with a clear idea, a suitable business model, and features that meet users’ needs.

If you are looking for mobile app design companies in Jeddah , it is important to know how to choose the right company, what to define before starting the project, and how to plan the app’s cost and expected return.
In this article, we explore the key decisions that can help turn an app idea into a scalable digital project, while introducing Nami’s mobile app design and development solutions.

An app design company does more than build screens and implement requested features. Its role also includes understanding the project idea and turning it into a digital experience that can be used and developed over time.
A company’s tasks typically include:
Idea analysis: Identifying the problem the app addresses and its target audience.
Feature definition: Selecting the core functions users need.
Interface design: Organizing screens and making services easy to access.
Software development: Building the app and connecting its functions and databases.
Testing: Ensuring features work correctly before launch.
Publication preparation: Preparing the app and its technical requirements for submission to the appropriate stores.

Nami is one of the leading providers of mobile app development services , turning ideas into innovative apps that combine professional design with strong performance to meet the needs of the Saudi market and help businesses strengthen their digital presence and achieve their commercial goals.
Before design and programming begin, you need to define how the app will deliver value to users and how the business will benefit from operating it.
Start by answering these questions:
What problem does the app solve? Does it save time, simplify purchases, organize bookings, or improve service delivery?
Who is the target user? Individuals, businesses, service providers, or a specific customer segment?
What is the current alternative? Do customers rely on a website, phone calls, or manual processes?
What will make the app useful? Identify a practical benefit that encourages users to choose it and return to it.
How will you measure success? Define measurable outcomes, such as completed orders, subscriptions, or active users.

This process helps you avoid developing features your audience does not need and direct your budget toward functions that deliver real value. Nami’s technical consulting services can help you assess project requirements and choose suitable technical solutions before implementation begins.
The right revenue model depends on the type of app, its audience, and the value it provides. Common models include:
This model suits e-commerce stores and apps that offer paid products or services. Revenue depends on sales, profit margins, order fulfillment costs, and customer acquisition costs.

This model can be used by apps that provide ongoing content or services in exchange for a monthly or annual subscription. It requires continuously delivering value that encourages users to stay subscribed.
This model suits apps that connect customers with service providers. The app earns a commission for each completed order or booking, according to the agreed business model.
Apps with a suitable user base can generate revenue through advertising or by selling additional features within the app, provided these methods do not negatively affect the user experience.
How do you choose the right model?
Identify whether your audience is willing to pay.
Calculate operating and user acquisition costs.
Compare expected revenue with ongoing expenses.
Test the model on a limited scale before expanding.
Review results and adjust the revenue approach when necessary.

Nami can help you develop a mobile app aligned with your business goals through carefully planned technical solutions that support a distinctive user experience and prepare your app to grow and benefit from revenue opportunities.

The required features vary according to the business and target audience. It is therefore best to focus on functions that make the app easier to use and support real business operations, rather than adding features without a clear need.
Features that may be useful for apps targeting the Saudi market include:
Arabic interface: Correctly supporting right-to-left (RTL) text direction.
Suitable payment options: Based on the business and the payment methods supported by the service provider.
Order and booking management: Tracking transactions and reducing errors.
Notifications: Informing users about important order updates, appointments, and offers.
Location services: When delivery or location-based services are needed.
Account and permission management: Protecting user data and controlling access to app functions.
Easy communication: Providing a clear channel for inquiries and support.
Device compatibility: Testing the app on the devices and operating system versions it targets.
These features should be selected according to the project. A commercial app does not necessarily need the same functions as a booking app or a field-service app.
Arabic apps require attention to interface details, not just translating text from one language to another. The way menus, buttons, numbers, and forms are displayed affects clarity and ease of use.
To improve the experience for Arabic-speaking users, consider the following:
Interface direction: Arrange elements to suit right-to-left text.
Clear wording: Use direct, easy-to-understand language.
Number and date formats: Choose formats appropriate for the app and its audience.
Simple forms: Organize registration fields, addresses, and contact details.
Relevant content: Use examples and information suited to the target market.
Real interface testing: Ensure elements do not overlap or appear in the wrong direction.
Nami’s design services can help create interfaces that match the project’s identity and users’ needs, with a focus on clear layouts and easy interaction.
A project may begin with a simple mobile app idea, but additional components may be needed to support efficient operations as the business grows.
For example, a project may include:
Customer app: For browsing services or products and placing orders.
Service provider or driver app: For receiving tasks and updating their status when needed.
Admin dashboard: For managing users, orders, content, and reports.
Backend and database: For processing, storing, and organizing information.
Website: For presenting information or providing services that complement the app. Nami’s website development services can help build websites suited to the project and its digital needs.
External integrations: Such as payment, shipping, or customer management systems.
You do not need to build all these components from the start. You can launch an initial version with core features, then add other components according to project needs and usage results.
One important technical decision is how to build the app, as this affects cost, maintenance, performance, and future development.
Native Development:
Build a separate app for each operating system.
Access system capabilities directly.
Suitable for projects that require specialized features or deep device integration.
May require more resources to develop and maintain apps for both systems.
Cross-Platform Development:
Use a technology that allows much of the code to be shared between Android and iOS.
Can reduce duplicated work in some projects.
Suitable for many apps that need to run on both systems.
May require additional solutions for certain specialized features.
Neither approach is best for every app. The choice depends on required functions, performance needs, budget, and the future development plan.
A clear contract helps organize the relationship between the client and the development company and prevent disputes over features, costs, and delivery.
Before signing, make sure the following points are clear:
Scope of work: The functions, screens, and systems included in the project.
Delivery stages: Expected deliverables at each stage.
Timeline: Estimated duration and conditions for changing it if requirements change.
Cost: Project price, payment terms, and potential additional costs.
Revisions: Number of review rounds and how change requests will be handled.
Ownership rights: Ownership of code, design, files, and accounts after handover.
Testing and acceptance: Criteria for approving the app before launch.
Maintenance and support: Support period, scope, and cost of additional services.
Confidentiality and data: Each party’s responsibilities regarding information and data used.
It is best to document any change in scope after work begins and clarify its impact on cost and timeline before approving it.
Finishing the programming does not mean the app is immediately ready for publication. Each store has requirements related to quality, privacy, content, and how the app is presented to users.
Before submission, review the following:
Ensure all functions are complete and there are no critical errors.
Test the app on the targeted devices and operating system versions.
Prepare the app name, description, icon, and screenshots.
Create a clear privacy policy that matches the data the app collects.
Review the permissions requested by the app and ensure they are necessary.
Provide test credentials if the app includes sign-in or restricted features.
Ensure links and support information work correctly.
Review the relevant store’s policies before submitting the app.

Apple’s App Review Guidelines highlight the importance of app completeness, reliable functionality, and clear information before review. You should also check current Google Play requirements based on the app type and features.

The cost of building a mobile app in Jeddah varies according to project size, required features, development approach, and the systems the app needs to connect to. Therefore, the scope of work should be defined before confirming the final price.
As a general guide, costs may fall into the following ranges:
Simple app: May start at around SAR 10,000 if its functions are limited.
Mid-range app: May cost between SAR 20,000 and SAR 50,000, depending on its requirements.
Advanced app: May cost SAR 60,000–120,000 or more when multiple features and integrations are needed.

These are general estimates, not actual quotations, and costs can vary significantly from one project to another. Prices should be confirmed with the development company based on the actual requirements.
The initial budget may include:
Idea analysis and scope definition.
Interface and user experience design.
Programming and feature development.
Admin dashboard and connected systems.
Testing and bug fixing.
Preparing app files for publication.
The budget does not end when the app is delivered. The project may have ongoing expenses, including:
Hosting and cloud services.
Fees for accounts or external services, where applicable.
Maintenance and updates.
Performance monitoring and troubleshooting.
Development of new features.
Marketing and user acquisition.
Nami’s cloud services help businesses use cloud solutions suited to the operation of digital systems, based on project requirements and the technical infrastructure in use.
For a realistic estimate, request a quotation that separates development costs from operating and maintenance expenses and identifies features that can be postponed to later phases.

You can reduce the risk of investing in an unsuitable idea by testing it before building the full app. The goal is to confirm that the audience has a real need and determine whether the proposed solution offers value worth using or paying for.
Follow these steps:
Talk to potential customers: Ask about the problem they face and how they currently deal with it.
Analyze existing alternatives: Review competing apps and identify what they offer and what they lack.
Define the minimum features: Select the essential functions needed to test the idea.
Create a prototype: Present the proposed screens and user journey before full development.
Test with users: Observe how clearly they understand the idea and how easily they complete key tasks.
Review the results: Adjust features or the business model based on feedback.
Develop gradually: Add other functions as the need becomes clear.
This approach helps identify problems early and direct resources toward the most important features instead of spending the budget on functions whose value has not been validated.

After launch, you need to monitor usage data to determine whether the app is delivering the desired results. Choose metrics based on the project’s main objective rather than relying on download numbers alone.
Key metrics include:
Active users: The number of people using the app during a defined period.
Order completion rate: The percentage of users who complete a purchase or booking.
User retention rate: Whether users return to the app.
Conversion rate: The percentage of users who complete the desired action.
Average order value: An important metric for sales-based apps.
Crash rate: A measure of app stability and issues that affect usage.
User ratings: A way to identify weaknesses and opportunities for improvement.
Regularly reviewing this data helps set priorities. The solution may be to simplify registration, improve app speed, or change how services are presented—not necessarily to add new features.

Nami offers integrated solutions that include:
App development: Building apps suited to your business and customers’ needs.
Design and user experience: Creating professional interfaces that make the app easier and more appealing to use.
Technical consulting: Choosing suitable technologies and defining project requirements before implementation.
Digital marketing: Using digital marketing services to increase reach among your target audience.
Future development: Preparing the app to accommodate new features as your business expands.

With Nami’s integrated digital services , you do not need to work with multiple providers for each part of your project. Instead, you can work with one technology partner that understands your goals and helps you move from idea to launch, then continue developing and growing.
Reviewing previous projects helps demonstrate how app requirements differ across industries. Visit Nami’s portfolio to explore examples of digital projects delivered by the company.
Examples include:
Maqani : A digital project for managing sheep information and tracking records.
Abu Battal for Sacrifices : An app for showcasing products and making orders easier.
Al Raji : A digital project for maintenance services and purchasing related supplies.
Sail Gates : A platform for presenting products and services and making them easier to access.
Real Estate Platform : A project for real estate services and property management.
Masahat Absher : A digital project related to property management and its services.

These examples illustrate the range of needs across digital projects and reinforce the importance of defining app functions according to the business rather than using the same model for every project.

If you are looking for a mobile app design company in Jeddah, start by defining your project idea, target audience, and how you will deliver services or generate revenue. You can then identify the core features, budget, and expected timeline.
Clear planning helps you discuss project requirements and evaluate technical solutions before implementation, while accounting for operating and development costs after launch.
You can contact Nami to discuss your idea and explore solutions suited to your project’s requirements, whether you are starting a new app or planning to develop an existing digital product.

Advertising and In-App Purchases Apps with a suitable user base can generate revenue through advertising or by selling additional features within the app, provided these methods do not negatively affect the user experience. How do you choose the right model? Identify whether your audience is willing to pay. Calculate operating and user acquisition costs. Compare expected revenue with ongoing expenses. Test the model on a limited scale before expanding. Review results and adjust the revenue approach when necessary. Mobile App Features Needed in the Saudi Market The required features vary according to the business and target audience. It is therefore best to focus on functions that make the app easier to use and support real business operations, rather than adding features without a clear need. Features that may be useful for apps targeting the Saudi market include: Arabic interface: Correctly supporting right-to-left (RTL) text direction. Suitable payment options: Based on the business and the payment methods supported by the service provider. Order and booking management: Tracking transactions and reducing errors. Notifications: Informing users about important order updates, appointments, and offers. Location services: When delivery or location-based services are needed. Account and permission management: Protecting user data and controlling access to app functions. Easy communication: Providing a clear channel for inquiries and support. Device compatibility: Testing the app on the devices and operating system versions it targets. These features should be selected according to the project. A commercial app does not necessarily need the same functions as a booking app or a field-service app. Arabic App Experience: RTL Support and Interfaces Suited to Saudi Users Arabic apps require attention to interface details, not just translating text from one language to another. The way menus, buttons, numbers, and forms are displayed affects clarity and ease of use. To improve the experience for Arabic-speaking users, consider the following: Interface direction: Arrange elements to suit right-to-left text. Clear wording: Use direct, easy-to-understand language. Number and date formats: Choose formats appropriate for the app and its audience. Simple forms: Organize registration fields, addresses, and contact details. Relevant content: Use examples and information suited to the target market. Real interface testing: Ensure elements do not overlap or appear in the wrong direction. Defining Your Digital Project’s Components A project may begin with a simple mobile app idea, but additional components may be needed to support efficient operations as the business grows. For example, a project may include: Customer app: For browsing services or products and placing orders. Service provider or driver app: For receiving tasks and updating their status when needed. Admin dashboard: For managing users, orders, content, and reports. Backend and database: For processing, storing, and organizing information. Website: For presenting information or providing services that complement the app. Nami’s website development services can help build websites suited to the project and its digital needs. External integrations: Such as payment, shipping, or customer management systems. You do not need to build all these components from the start. You can launch an initial version with core features, then add other components according to project needs and usage results. How Do You Choose Between Native and Cross-Platform Development? One important technical decision is how to build the app, as this affects cost, maintenance, performance, and future development. Native Development: Build a separate app for each operating system. Access system capabilities directly. Suitable for projects that require specialized features or deep device integration. May require more resources to develop and maintain apps for both systems. Cross-Platform Development: Use a technology that allows much of the code to be shared between Android and iOS. Can reduce duplicated work in some projects. Suitable for many apps that need to run on both systems. May require additional solutions for certain specialized features. Neither approach is best for every app. The choice depends on required functions, performance needs, budget, and the future development plan. What Should a Mobile App Design and Development Contract Include? A clear contract helps organize the relationship between the client and the development company and prevent disputes over features, costs, and delivery. Before signing, make sure the following points are clear: Scope of work: The functions, screens, and systems included in the project. Delivery stages: Expected deliverables at each stage. Timeline: Estimated duration and conditions for changing it if requirements change. Cost: Project price, payment terms, and potential additional costs. Revisions: Number of review rounds and how change requests will be handled. Ownership rights: Ownership of code, design, files, and accounts after handover. Testing and acceptance: Criteria for approving the app before launch. Maintenance and support: Support period, scope, and cost of additional services. Confidentiality and data: Each party’s responsibilities regarding information and data used. It is best to document any change in scope after work begins and clarify its impact on cost and timeline before approving it. Preparing Your App for Publication on Google Play and the App Store Finishing the programming does not mean the app is immediately ready for publication. Before submission, review the following: Ensure all functions are complete and there are no critical errors. Test the app on the targeted devices and operating system versions. Prepare the app name, description, icon, and screenshots. Create a clear privacy policy that matches the data the app collects. Review the permissions requested by the app and ensure they are necessary. Provide test credentials if the app includes sign-in or restricted features. Ensure links and support information work correctly. How Can You Test Your App Idea Before Investing a Large Budget? You can reduce the risk of investing in an unsuitable idea by testing it before building the full app. The goal is to confirm that the audience has a real need and determine whether the proposed solution offers value worth using or paying for. Follow these steps: Talk to potential customers: Ask about the problem they face and how they currently deal with it. Analyze existing alternatives: Review competing apps and identify what they offer and what they lack. Define the minimum features: Select the essential functions needed to test the idea. Create a prototype: Present the proposed screens and user journey before full development. Test with users: Observe how clearly they understand the idea and how easily they complete key tasks. Review the results: Adjust features or the business model based on feedback. Develop gradually: Add other functions as the need becomes clear. This approach helps identify problems early and direct resources toward the most important features instead of spending the budget on functions whose value has not been validated. Metrics That Show Whether Your App Is Achieving Its Business Goals After launch, you need to monitor usage data to determine whether the app is delivering the desired results. Crash rate: A measure of app stability and issues that affect usage. User ratings: A way to identify weaknesses and opportunities for improvement. Regularly reviewing this data helps set priorities.
